subject: Order Form: opt-out window and TFC carve-in discussion
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@skyvault.io>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skyvault.io
Date: 2026-05-18 09:12 PDT
Subject: Draft Order Form — notice window & TFC questions

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending the draft. Two items Procurement flagged in our internal review: 1) the auto-renew notice is 60 days — they'd like 45 days for pilot/POC deals, and 2) the "Termination for Convenience" (TFC) language seems broad; Procurement wants either an explicit offboarding window or a proportional termination fee if we exercise early termination.

High level ask: can Redwood give us a shorter opt-out window for the pilot (45 days) and a TFC carve that guarantees data handoff/30-day post-termination support (or a one-time fee), so our internal stakeholders can approve quickly? We prefer to keep the MSA unchanged but are open to an order-form-level carve.

We're on a tight timeline — can you loop in legal/ops if there's anything that needs counter-signature?

Appreciate it,
Alex
Procurement Lead — SkyVault

Attachments: SkyVault_review_notes_0518.pdf (attachment stub)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Alex Mercer <alex@skyvault.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-18 10:03 PDT
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form — notice window & TFC questions

Alex — thanks, and great context.

Short answer: yes, we can discuss an order-form carve that shortens the opt-out window for pilot customers and surface a limited TFC mechanism tied to an offboarding commitment. I attached a redline of the order form showing two alternative approaches:

Option A (preferred for pilots): 45-day notice to non-renew the initial term; no change to the MSA auto-renew section but this order form supersedes for the pilot term.

Option B (if legal pushes back): retain 60-day notice but add a 30-day post-termination transition support obligation plus a one-time termination processing fee equal to 10% of remaining committed fees.

Can you confirm which route Procurement prefers? If Procurement accepts Option A, we can keep the MSA untouched and proceed. If they want Option B, I'll ask Legal to weigh in on the proportional fee language.

Looping in Karthik (sales/legal interface) and Marissa (contracts) to advise on risk and preferred drafting.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0126

Attachments: SkyVault_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (redline with both options)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Alex Mercer <alex@skyvault.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-18 13:25 PDT
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form — notice window & TFC questions

Thanks for looping me in. Quick thoughts from a sales/legal operations POV:

- Option A (45-day pilot opt-out) is operationally acceptable but increases churn risk if we don't require a small ramp-down fee or a firm offboarding plan. Recommend pairing 45-day opt-out with a mandatory "offboarding schedule" (deliverables + timelines) in the order form.

- Option B (60-day + 30-day transition + 10% processing fee) is defensible contractually and simpler for us to enforce. The 10% figure is negotiable; I'd prefer a fixed service-fee cap (e.g., max $25k) so large TCV deals don't balloon the fee.

Practical proposal: For pilots under $100k TCV, use Option A + offboarding schedule. For anything above $100k, default to Option B with a cap on the fee. That keeps procurement happy on small deals and preserves protections on larger accounts.

Marissa — can you confirm whether the order-form language can reference a separate "Offboarding Annex" to avoid MSA changes?

-Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, Alex Mercer <alex@skyvault.io>
Date: 2026-05-18 15:10 PDT
Subject: Re: Draft Order Form — notice window & TFC questions

Hi all — legal review quick note.

We can do an order-form carve without amending the MSA by adding a new Order Form section titled "Pilot Term & Offramp" that states: 1) pilot term will auto-renew unless Customer provides written notice at least 45 days prior to term end; and 2) Customer or Redwood may terminate the pilot for convenience with 30 days' written notice, during which Redwood will provide transition assistance as set forth in an attached Offboarding Annex.

If Redwood agrees to a termination processing fee, keep the fee language outside the MSA and specify a fee schedule in the Order Form (e.g., 10% of remaining fees, capped at $25,000). Avoid open-ended "TFC" wording that could imply unlimited liability — keep obligations limited to transition activities and return/deletion of Customer data.

One redline comment: ensure we include an SLA carve for the 30-day transition so customers can't claim breach of service for scheduled offboarding activities.

I updated the redline to include the Offboarding Annex placeholder and fee cap. See attached redline-summary.docx.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
